answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation, then slash that stake when independently verified fraud is proven. One person can still mint many identities, but each must tie up capital, and a lantern-like audit trail links claims to outcomes so honest peers can challenge them. A juniper-themed profile or a wharf address earns no extra trust: the attacker pays the bond for every Sybil and risks losing it.
